process.title: How Barangay Tumana Handles Complaints
process.subtitle: From submitting your grievance to final resolution, track every official stage transparently under Republic Act No. 7160.
process.step1_desc: Create a resident account or visit Barangay Tumana Hall. Provide your narrative, incident details, the people involved, and any supporting files.
process.step2_desc: The Lupon Intake & Screening Officer (LISO) reviews whether the dispute falls under Barangay Tumana KP jurisdiction, verifies party information, confirms up to 2 complaint categories, and marks valid filings Approved (or asks for missing details).
process.step3_desc: Before formal docketing, the Barangay Secretary or Clerk schedules a polite informal invitation (Paanyaya) giving both parties a chance for private, constructive dialogue and early voluntary settlement.
process.step4_desc: If unresolved during Paanyaya or a party fails to appear, the case is officially docketed and formal Summons (KP Form 9) are served for Mediation presided over by the Punong Barangay within the statutory 15-day period.
process.step5_desc: If Mediation does not settle the dispute, a three-member Pangkat Tagapagkasundo is constituted from the Lupon to hold formal Conciliation hearings (15 days, extendible up to 15 more days), or conduct Arbitration upon written mutual agreement.
process.step6_desc: Depending on hearing results and statutory rules, the case concludes under one of these official dispositions:
process.outcome_settled_desc: Signed KP Form 16 or Arbitration Award carrying the force of a final court judgment after 10 days.
process.outcome_repudiated_desc: Sworn statement filed within 10 days only when consent was vitiated by fraud, violence, or intimidation.
process.outcome_cfa_desc: Issued if no settlement is reached after mandatory KP stages (or willful default), allowing filing in court.
process.outcome_dismissed_desc: Closed when outside KP jurisdiction, withdrawn, barred, or dismissed due to complainant non-appearance.

mv.title: Our Vision & Mission
mv.subtitle: Guided by the official charter of the Katarungang Pambarangay — Lupong Tagapamayapa of Barangay Tumana, Marikina City under RA 7160.
mv.vision_heading: An Orderly, Peaceful, Joyful, and United Barangay Tumana
mv.vision_body: Now and in the future, the Lupong Tagapamayapa, through resolving community matters with integrity and wisdom, strives to achieve an orderly, peaceful, joyful, and united Barangay Tumana.
mv.vision_official_text: “Ngayon at sa hinaharap, ang Lupong Tagapamayapa, sa pamamagitan ng may integridad at talinong pagresolba sa mga usaping pang-komunidad; nagsusumikap na makamit ang isang maayos, mapayapa, masaya at nagkakaisang Barangay Tumana.”
mv.mission_heading: Prompt, Fair, and Integrity-Driven Community Justice
mv.mission_body: It is the mission of the Lupong Tagapamayapa of Barangay Tumana to provide prompt and peaceful settlement of community challenges through an open, fair, and integrity-driven service, and to be an effective partner of the Courts and Homeowners' Associations (HOA) in de-escalating cases in accordance with the mandate of Republic Act 7160, Local Government Code of 1991.
mv.mission_official_text: “Misyon ng Lupong Tagapamayapa ng Barangay Tumana na makapagbigay ng isang maagap at mapayapang pag-aayos ng mga hamong pang-komunidad sa pamamagitan ng isang bukas, patas at may integridad na serbisyo at maging epektibong katuwang ng Korte at ng HOA sa pagpapababa ng kaso nang naaayon sa mandato ng Republic Act 7160, Local Government Code of 1991.”

faq.title: Answers About Filing & Barangay Hearings
faq.subtitle: Helpful information for Barangay Tumana residents before submitting a complaint or attending a Lupon session.
faq.cta_title: Ready to file or check your case?
faq.cta_desc: Register with your email address or sign in to track your complaint status and hearing schedule.
faq.q1: How do I create an account and file a complaint online?
faq.a1: Create a resident account, sign in, and select Submit a concern on your dashboard. Follow the preliminary screening status from the same dashboard.
faq.q2: What disputes are covered under Katarungang Pambarangay (RA 7160)?
faq.a2: Generally, disputes between individuals residing in Marikina City (following Barangay Tumana territorial jurisdiction rules under Section 409 of RA 7160) involving civil matters or minor criminal offenses punishable by not more than one (1) year imprisonment or a fine not exceeding ₱5,000 are handled here. During review, LISO screens jurisdiction—disputes involving non-negotiable criminal cases, urgent court relief, or excluded parties may be referred or closed accordingly.
faq.q3: What is the difference between Paanyaya, Mediation, and Conciliation?
faq.a3: Paanyaya is an informal pre-docket dialogue scheduled by the Barangay Secretary/Clerk to help both parties settle early without formal summons. If unresolved, the case moves to Mediation presided over by the Punong Barangay with official Summons (KP Form 9) for up to 15 days. If still unsettled, a three-member Pangkat Tagapagkasundo leads formal Conciliation hearings for 15 days (extendible up to 15 more days), or Arbitration if both parties agree in writing.
faq.q4: Can I dictate my complaint narrative?
faq.a4: Yes. Open Dictate with Gemini, record your narrative, and review and edit the transcript before adding it to the complaint.
faq.q5: How do I know my current complaint stage and hearing schedule?
faq.a5: Sign in to your Resident Portal using your username or email address. Your dashboard and case record show your exact live stage (For Review, Approved, Paanyaya, Mediation, Conciliation, Arbitration, Settled, Repudiated, For CFA, CFA, or Dismissed) along with your assigned Paanyaya or Lupon hearing schedules.
faq.q6: What happens if the respondent ignores Paanyaya or if we still do not settle?
faq.a6: If a party does not attend informal Paanyaya, the Lupon proceeds with formal docketing and official Summons (KP Form 9) for Punong Barangay Mediation. If no agreement is reached through Mediation and Pangkat Conciliation—or if a settlement is validly repudiated within 10 days—the Lupon issues a Certificate to File Action (CFA) so the complainant can bring the case to court or the prosecutor's office.
faq.q7: Can I still file a complaint if I prefer walk-in assistance?
faq.a7: Yes. Residents without internet access or preferring personal assistance may file directly at the Office of the Punong Barangay / Lupon Secretariat in Barangay Tumana Hall. Walk-in complaints are also recorded in AGAP so your case details and hearing notices remain organized.
